_comment: Ratchet baseline for the Datastore Isolation workflow (TD-881).
max_data_carrying is a CEILING THAT MAY ONLY EVER FALL. CI fails when a run
exceeds it, which is the signal that something new in the suite reaches the
operator's real services. When a run comes in under it, lower this number so
the ground gained cannot be given back.
It is not zero, and that is deliberate. Zero would require every test that
spawns a real hook script to be re-pointed at a throwaway instance -- roughly
eighteen more files, tracked separately as a burn-down. What protects the
operator today is the network namespace: every one of these connections lands
on the tripwire inside the namespace and reaches nothing real. This number
measures test hygiene; the namespace provides the safety.
Measured on the CI-scope suite (-m 'not regression and not quarantine') with
a cleared environment, inside unshare -rn, ordering fixed via -p no:randomly.
Two consecutive runs gave 228 and 229; the variance is gRPC retry jitter on
26351. The ceiling carries a small allowance over the observed maximum so
that jitter alone cannot fail the gate.
Before this work the same measurement was 147 accepts / 122 data-carrying
across the three ports then being watched, with 101 on the Qdrant REST port
that tests write through. That port now sits at 4. The total rose only
because Langfuse (23100) was added to the watched set and turned out to
account for 204 connections that had never been measured before.

pre_fix_reference.note: Same command before this work; 23100 was not yet watched.
